title: Chicken thigh, baked or broiled, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thigh is the dark‑meat portion of the bird, generally juicier and more flavorful than breast meat. In fast‑food or restaurant settings it is often baked in the oven or grilled, with the skin left on and eaten, adding extra taste and calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thigh meat contains more fat than breast, which makes it more tender when cooked.
The skin is rich in collagen that turns into gelatin during cooking.
Fast‑food kitchens frequently marinate thighs in soy sauce, spices, and a touch of sugar for a caramelized crust.
Baking at 180‑200 °C yields a crispy skin while keeping the meat moist.
Chicken thighs are commonly served with barbecue, honey‑mustard, or spicy sauces.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B6 and niacin (B3), important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals help form hemoglobin and support immune health.

items.title: Skin supplies healthy fats
items.content: The skin’s fat includes monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that can benefit heart health when eaten in moderation.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Thighs with skin are more calorie‑dense than skinless breast, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: The skin contains saturated fat; excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor Salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Chicken protein allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken thigh can be eaten on its own, sliced into salads, added to sandwiches, or mixed into pasta dishes. The skin is usually left on for crispness, but can be removed if a lower‑fat option is desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chicken thigh in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it keeps quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
